paragraphs.title: The Oil Miracle and the Rescue of the Prophet’s Family

easy.explanation: The widow cried unto Elisha because of her family’s debt.
easy.q: To whom did the widow cry for help?

answers: They would be taken as bondmen
They would be sent to another city
easy.explanation: The creditor had come to take her two sons to be bondmen.
easy.q: What danger did the widow’s two sons face?

easy.explanation: She said that she had nothing save a pot of oil.
easy.q: What did the widow have in her house?

answers: So the oil could be poured into them
So she could sell the vessels
So she could cook for her sons
medium.explanation: The empty vessels were needed to receive the multiplying oil.
medium.q: Why did Elisha tell the woman to borrow vessels from her neighbours?

medium.explanation: She poured the oil into the vessels as her sons brought them.
medium.q: What did the woman do while her sons brought the vessels?

medium.explanation: The vessels were empty containers that could be filled with oil.
medium.q: In the KJV, what is a “vessel” in this passage?

answers: The oil in the pot ran out
The neighbours took back their vessels
challenge.explanation: The oil stayed when her son said, “There is not a vessel more.”
challenge.q: What caused the oil to stop flowing?

answers: She sold it, paid the debt, and lived on the rest
She gave it directly to the creditor
She kept it only for household use
challenge.explanation: Elisha told her to sell the oil, pay her debt, and live on the remainder.
challenge.q: How did the oil solve the family’s trouble?

answers: The miracle took place inside the woman’s house
The sons were forbidden to help
The neighbours were not allowed to lend vessels
challenge.explanation: The woman poured the oil inside with the door shut upon her and her sons.
challenge.q: What did shutting the door emphasize?

paragraphs.title: The Shunammite Woman’s Hospitality and the Birth of Her Son

easy.explanation: Elisha passed to Shunem, where the great woman lived.
easy.q: From what place was the woman who welcomed Elisha?

answers: She constrained him to eat bread
She sent him to the king
easy.explanation: She welcomed Elisha to eat bread whenever he passed by.
easy.q: What did the woman regularly do when Elisha passed by?

answers: A bed, a table, a stool, and a candlestick
A pot, a bowl, and a jar
A gate, a wall, and a throne
easy.explanation: She prepared a bed, table, stool, and candlestick for Elisha.
easy.q: What furnishings did she prepare in the chamber?

answers: So he would have a place to stay when he passed by
So he could teach her son
So he could guard her house
medium.explanation: Elisha passed by continually, so she prepared a room for him.
medium.q: Why did the woman want to make Elisha a chamber?

answers: Speak for her to the king or the captain of the host
medium.explanation: Gehazi asked whether she should be spoken for to the king or the captain of the host.
medium.q: What did Gehazi suggest Elisha could do for the woman?

answers: A woman of wealth or high standing
medium.explanation: Her home and generous hospitality suggest that she was a woman of standing and means.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “a great woman” most nearly mean?

answers: She was content to dwell among her own people
She wanted to move to another country
challenge.explanation: She answered, “I dwell among mine own people.”
challenge.q: What did the woman’s refusal to ask the king or captain reveal?

answers: She had no child, and her husband was old
She had specifically requested a son
She was poor and needed an heir
challenge.explanation: Gehazi told Elisha that she had no child and that her husband was old.
challenge.q: What led Gehazi to suggest that she might receive a son?

answers: The woman conceived and bare a son at the appointed season
The son was born that same day
challenge.explanation: The woman bore a son at the season Elisha had spoken of.

paragraphs.title: The Child’s Death and the Shunammite Woman’s Appeal to Elisha

easy.explanation: The child went out to his father to the reapers.
easy.q: Where did the child go with his father?
What did the child complain about?

answers: On the bed of the man of God
easy.explanation: She laid him on the bed of the man of God and shut the door.
easy.q: Where did the mother lay the child?

answers: So she could quickly go to the man of God
So she could search for her husband
medium.explanation: She wanted to run to Elisha and return.
medium.q: Why did the Shunammite ask for an ass and a young man?

answers: I am going to the king
medium.explanation: She answered briefly, “It shall be well.”
medium.q: What did she answer when her husband asked why she was going?

medium.explanation: To saddle the ass was to prepare it for the journey.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does “saddled an ass” mean?

answers: She did not know what had happened
She was angry with her son
challenge.explanation: She laid the child down, prepared to travel, and went directly to Elisha.
challenge.q: What does the woman’s first response to the child’s death show?

answers: To learn whether they were well
To invite them to a feast
To send them before the king
challenge.explanation: Elisha instructed Gehazi to ask whether each of them was well.
challenge.q: Why did Elisha tell Gehazi to ask about the woman, her husband, and the child?

answers: She was determined that Elisha should go with her
She agreed to send only Gehazi
challenge.explanation: She refused to leave Elisha until he arose and followed her.
challenge.q: What did her words, “I will not leave thee,” show?

paragraphs.title: The Revival of the Shunammite’s Son

easy.explanation: Elisha sent Gehazi ahead with his staff.
easy.q: Who was first sent to the child with Elisha’s staff?

answers: There was neither voice nor hearing
The child spoke to his mother
easy.explanation: Gehazi reported that there was neither voice nor hearing.
easy.q: What happened when Gehazi laid the staff on the child’s face?

easy.explanation: The child sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.
easy.q: How many times did the child sneeze?

medium.explanation: Elisha shut the door and prayed unto the LORD.
medium.q: What did Elisha do before lying upon the child?

medium.explanation: He put his mouth upon the child’s mouth, his eyes upon his eyes, and his hands upon his hands.
medium.q: Which parts of Elisha’s body did he place upon the child’s?

medium.explanation: The child’s flesh became warm as Elisha lay upon him.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does “waxed warm” mean?

answers: The staff had produced no response
Gehazi refused to enter the room
The mother asked to remain alone
challenge.explanation: Because there was neither voice nor hearing, Elisha entered and prayed himself.
challenge.q: Why did Elisha act after Gehazi’s attempt?

challenge.explanation: The child’s flesh waxed warm before he sneezed and opened his eyes.
challenge.q: What was the first sign that the child was responding?

answers: Elisha returned her son to her
The mother sent the child to his father
challenge.explanation: Elisha told her, “Take up thy son,” and she carried him out.
challenge.q: How did the meeting between the mother and child end?

paragraphs.title: The Rescue of the Prophetic Disciples During Famine

easy.explanation: The passage says there was a dearth in the land.
easy.q: What was in the land when Elisha returned to Gilgal?

easy.explanation: Elisha said, “Set on the great pot, and seethe pottage.”
easy.q: What did Elisha tell his servant to prepare?

easy.explanation: He gathered wild gourds from a wild vine.
easy.q: What did the man gather from the field?

answers: The pottage seemed poisonous and they could not eat it
medium.explanation: They feared the gathered gourds had made the pottage dangerous.
medium.q: Why did the men cry, “O thou man of God, there is death in the pot”?

medium.explanation: Elisha said, “Then bring meal,” and cast it into the pot.
medium.q: What did Elisha tell them to put into the pot?

medium.explanation: Pottage is food cooked together in a pot.

answers: Wild gourds were gathered without knowing what they were
There was no meal in the pot
challenge.explanation: The man gathered wild gourds, “for they knew them not.”
challenge.q: Why did the pottage become dangerous?

answers: There was no harm in the pot
challenge.explanation: After the meal was added, the people could eat and there was no harm in the pot.
challenge.q: What changed after the meal was added?

answers: The shortage led them to gather unfamiliar food
The famine caused the pot to break
The famine forced the prophets to leave
challenge.explanation: Because of the famine, the men searched the field for food and gathered what they did not recognize.
challenge.q: What connection does the famine have with this event?

paragraphs.title: The Miracle of the Bread and Grain

easy.q: Where did the man who brought the bread come from?

easy.explanation: He brought twenty loaves of barley.
easy.q: How many barley loaves did he bring?

easy.explanation: The servant questioned how the food could be set before one hundred men.

answers: The amount seemed too small for one hundred men
There was no food at all
Elisha had forbidden them to eat
medium.explanation: The servant wondered how the small supply could feed one hundred men.
medium.q: Why did the servant question giving the food to the people?

answers: They would eat and leave thereof
medium.explanation: Elisha said, “They shall eat, and shall leave thereof.”
medium.q: What did Elisha say would happen according to the word of the LORD?

answers: Fresh grain still in its husk
medium.explanation: The man brought full ears of corn in the husk together with the barley loaves.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “full ears of corn” describe?

answers: The people ate and left food afterward
challenge.explanation: The people ate and left thereof, according to the word of the LORD.
challenge.q: What proves that the miracle took place?

answers: A small amount of food and one hundred men
A large house and a small house
An old man and a child
challenge.explanation: Twenty barley loaves and grain were set before one hundred men.
challenge.q: What is the central contrast in this event?

answers: The result happened as the LORD had said
The food came from the field
The servant spoke for the people
challenge.explanation: The concluding phrase confirms that the people ate and had leftovers as promised.
challenge.q: What does “according to the word of the LORD” emphasize?
